where: Section 2, bullet on reading properties from a point
problem: "Read ... enthalpy along the local wet-bulb line" suggests enthalpy is constant along a wet-bulb line and can be read by scanning along it. The enthalpy line through the point is a separate line that only lies nearly along the wet-bulb line; along a constant wet-bulb line the enthalpy actually falls slightly. A student can misread this as the trap already warned about in a different form.
fix: Read enthalpy from the enthalpy line that passes through the point. On most charts these lines lie almost, but not exactly, along the wet-bulb lines, so do not slide along a wet-bulb line to pick up enthalpy.

problem: Wet-bulb temperature is listed as a property that the chart gives and is used throughout, but it is never defined anywhere in the chapter.
fix: Add one line at first use: the wet-bulb temperature is the steady temperature shown by a small thermometer whose bulb is kept wet in a fast stream of the air; the ordinary air temperature is then called the dry-bulb temperature.
